newsitem.title: USA: Yellen sees no inflation in latest jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Yellen sees no inflation in latest jobs data.

text.p: White House economic adviser Janet Yellen on Friday said the unemployment data for March showed balanced growth with no evidence that inflation was breaking out.
Interviewed on CNBC, Yellen conceded that labor markets were tight and bore watching.
"Labor markets are tight and that bears watching but I don't see any evidence in today's report of any inflationary pressure there," she said.
She said that the four percent increase in average hourly earnings over the past year translated into a real pace of wage increase that is consistent with the rise in productivity.
Yellen said also that she preferred to look at total compensation rather than average hourly earnings in assessing inflation.
"Total compensation has been running at a pace that is clearly consistent with stable inflation," she said.
Asked about talks between the administration and the congress on a balanced budget agreement, Yellen said they have been good and that she was optimistic about chances that a deal can be struck.
